review_plan.claim_under_review: As produced by driver.py analysis on RUN-SDEG-3de103: validity completed_valid; outcome_C7 = B. B1 (A1 serial-split subresultant PRS, field-form pseudo-remainder per v4 D-1) has total-work beta_work worst ~0.797 on interval_x and random_x and ~0.647 on subgroup_x, 95% CIs far above the 0.30 gate; B0 calibration ~0.59-0.67; beta_elim(interval_x) ~0.598 (pre-registered ~3/5); W_triple beta ~1.0. Scope: L in {8,16,32}, 3 seeds, decks interval_x/subgroup_x/random_x + progression control, the Mac, one worker.
review_plan.coordinator_prior: I expect J1 to PASS (the implementation was audited and re-checked, and the run self-reports clean agreement). I expect outcome B to stand but ONLY for A1 as metered here: the red team will argue (correctly) that it closes nothing beyond L<=32 and this meter, that W_triple beta ~1.0 means the per-triple PRS cost tracks |T| ~ q, so the early-abort subresultant route cannot beat the eliminant, and that subgroup_x's all-median 0.358 is an artifact of the median over mixed members/non-members. I also already saw an informal validator slope ~0.80 (AMD-20260928-d3ed9e), so my prior is contaminated toward B; this is disclosed, and reviewers should weigh it.

joints.joint: J1 run integrity: manifest/admission/plan/amendment hashes; 36/36 cells complete; oracle/B0/B1 decision agreement and equal hit-triple sets on every query; audit accepted; B2 split and FGLM checks; compressed_cells.json round-trip; the failed attempt RUN-SDEG-5484a4 contributes nothing; beta values reproduced from raw-result.json by an independent re-computation of the frozen statistic.
joints.attack_plan: Decompress the three .zst cells and verify sha256. Recompute every beta_work(B0/B1) worst/median point and bootstrap CI from per-query W in raw-result.json with your own script from the specification's definition (log W vs log q over sizes), and diff against metrics.json. Grep all cells for any query with a B0/B1 disagreement, a watchdog stop or a lower-bound flag. I think it breaks, if anywhere, in the worst-statistic definition or the per-size log q used.
joints.breaking_artifact: a query or statistic where recomputation differs from metrics.json beyond bootstrap noise, or any unrecorded disagreement/watchdog

joints.joint: J2 interpretation and scope: does outcome B follow for A1 as specified in RT-1476 (inputs/idea_generation_20260718_batch2.md lines 88-212), and what exactly does it close?
joints.attack_plan: (a) Show whether B1's charged work is dominated by a term the A1 idea would not pay (e.g. W_fixed_xR, table building, non-amortized per-query setup); compute beta on W_triple and on W minus W_fixed_xR from raw-result.json. (b) Argue whether the field-form PRS or the early-abort order could make B1 costlier than A1 needs. (c) State the smallest change to A1 that the data does NOT rule out (amortized table across queries, different split, index calculus over a factor base) as forward guidance. (d) Check the extrapolation risk: is the L-range long enough that a q^{0.3} term hidden under a larger low-order term would be invisible? I expect it breaks at (a) only if W_fixed dominates, which W_triple beta ~1.0 argues against.
joints.breaking_artifact: a computation from the run's own data showing beta for the A1-relevant cost below 0.30, or a named cost B1 pays that A1 does not
